content:
Apple Podcasts has long been my go-to podcast app, but for a long time, I've been quite frustrated with its core "Up Next" playlist feature. I'm happy to share that iOS 27.2 brings a solution.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts' "Up Next" playlist into two parts: "New Episodes" and "Keep Listening".

There's a lot to like about Apple Podcasts. Transcripts and auto-generated chapters are two killer features that make this app my favourite choice. I've also been enjoying all the recent video-related upgrades.

But for years, Apple Podcasts' core "Up Next" playlist has frequently made me want to switch to another app.

I've previously written about why the "Up Next" feature is flawed. In short:

  • It makes it hard to clearly see what new episodes are available to listen to.
  • Episodes easily disappear, even if you've already listened to half of them.

But I'm excited to share that iOS 27.2 finally brings the long-awaited solution to "Up Next". The method is splitting this feature into two separate parts:

  • New Episodes
  • Keep Listening

At the very top of the app is "New Episodes", which looks and functions similarly to the old "Up Next". As the name suggests, it only displays the latest episode of every show you follow.

"Keep Listening" sits right below it, serving as a central hub where you can find all the episodes you've started but haven't finished.

Top comment from Nutmac

Playlist management is still a mess, and the inability to sync across devices is really baffling.

Together, these two sections address all my major issues with the old "Up Next" playlist.

You can easily see at a glance what's new, and I haven't lost any episodes because anything I start listening to appears in "Keep Listening". I still have some minor quibbles, but these changes alone have solved my main issues with "Up Next".

If you haven't tried Apple Podcasts in a while, iOS 27.2 is a great time to give it another chance.

Do you use Apple or another podcast app? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
